video.title: 6 Ways to Make Money With the New GPT Agent (It Blew My Mind)

summary: Chris Koerner demos OpenAI's new ChatGPT Agent mode, running six agents at once on business tasks: finding Nashville plumbers with websites, hyper-personalised cold emails to Austin dentists, competitor research for his Texas Snacks store, Google Trends ranking of business ideas, a calendar meeting-briefing task, and Amazon-review research that became a pitch deck. He pitches selling websites or SEO to businesses that already have websites, and selling AI-driven research to clients. He rates each task out of 10 and notes friction: logins, glitches when he navigated away from the tab, and slow runs. Takeaway: agents save hours of research and drafting, but need specific prompts, reference data and some supervision.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; owns Texas Snacks e-commerce store; runs TK Owners community

ideas.name: Websites for businesses that already have websites
ideas.one_liner: Build or redesign websites for local business owners who already have a site, because they value having one.
ideas.business_model: One-off project fees for website builds or redesigns
ideas.customer: Local business owners (e.g. plumbers) who already have a website
ideas.problem: Existing sites are statistically likely to be poor; owners who value a site will pay to improve it
ideas.offer: Website build or redesign, with AI making delivery more profitable

acquisition_channels.details: Use ChatGPT Agent to find 20 plumbers in Nashville with websites, collect owner emails and phones, then write personalised emails. Directories like Manta used for hard-to-find contact info.

quote.text: We want to find business owners that already have websites. We don't need to assume or guess that it's an ugly website because statistically speaking, it probably is.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Build websites for clients, with AI making it more profitable; details not stated

acquisition.how: Agent builds lead lists and drafts emails, but the agent took about 30 minutes for 20 leads and glitched. UK sole traders cannot be cold-emailed under PECR, so outreach is limited to limited companies and needs checking.

onboarding.how: Briefing and scoping calls need a human, with tooling help.

delivery.how: AI site builders and agents can produce most of a site, with human review.

billing.how: Invoicing and payment links are easy to automate.

support.how: Edit requests and client handholding need some human involvement.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK. Cold email must target limited companies only, not sole traders (PECR).

risks: Many small-business owners are pitched websites constantly
Cold email to sole traders is illegal in the UK without consent
Agent lead lists can be slow and error-prone

quotes.text: I think one business idea that exists today, existed 10 years ago, and will exist in another 10 years is simply making websites for other people.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Hyper-personalised SEO for niche professionals (Austin dentists)
ideas.one_liner: Agent-researched, personalised cold emails selling SEO to dentists in one city.
ideas.problem: Poor local search ranking (e.g. not on page one for South Austin implants)
ideas.offer: SEO services exclusively for Austin dentists

acquisition_channels.details: Agent researched five dentists (education, hobbies, pets) and drafted personalised emails into Gmail drafts. The demo took about 3 minutes of research, and subject lines needed fixing. Chris says he doesn't actually sell SEO.

quote.text: Make a list of five dentists in Austin, owners only. Write five cold emails that are hyperpersonalized to each of them.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition.how: Research and drafting are automated, but the agent needs logins, glitches, and supervision. Dentists are often sole traders or partnerships, which PECR restricts for cold email.

delivery.how: SEO work is tool-heavy, not covered in the video.

support.how: Client reporting and calls need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Works with changes: many UK dentists are sole traders or partnerships, so PECR restricts cold email. Corporate practices are fair game.

risks: PECR breach if emailing sole traders

quotes.text: I don't have to hire anyone to do my cold emails anymore. I just need to prompt it and then log in.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Selling competitive research reports and implementation
ideas.one_liner: Use an AI agent to research a company's competitors, then sell the report or help implement it as a consultant.

ideas.delivery: Agent produces the research report, and the consultant can then implement

onboarding.how: A form can collect the URL and goals.

delivery.how: Agent produced the report on his own site; the output needs a human sanity check.

support.how: Follow-up questions can be answered by AI.

quotes.text: even if you don't already own a business, you can use a prompt like this to do competitive research on other companies and then you can sell them that research

tactics.name: Target businesses that already have websites
steps: Pick a local trade and city
Have the agent find businesses that already have websites and list owner contact info
Skip judging the site quality; having a site signals they value it

quote.text: if you go give this same offer to business owners that don't have a website, they could have one by now.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Give the agent reference data and name sources
steps: Provide examples (e.g. four sample ideas) so output matches your taste
Name specific sources such as Manta, Reddit, Facebook, X and niche blogs
Say 'move fast' to speed it up
Ask for niche, specific case studies to avoid generic articles

quote.text: Anytime you ask it to do a task or to return something interesting for you, give it reference data.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Mine Amazon reviews for product gaps
steps: Ask the agent to research reviews for similar products
Extract common complaints and rank by proportion with a pie chart
Create a feature list addressing the top pain points
Turn findings into a pitch deck

quote.text: I don't want to fix problems that are anecdotal and don't affect a large percentage of people.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Run multiple agents in parallel and minimise logins
steps: Open several agent tabs for independent tasks
Avoid tasks needing account logins where possible
Do not navigate away from tabs inside logged-in accounts
Ask for CSV export if Google Sheets glitches

quote.text: The less you ask it to log in for now, the better.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Case-study-to-launch-plan prompt
steps: Have the agent rank low-cost ideas using Google Trends
Pick one and request niche case studies with startup costs and early sales
Ask for 40 stories, then a 30-day launch plan

quote.text: Come up with a dayby-day launch plan over the next 30 days.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Specific prompts with named sources and reference examples beat generic prompts.

quote.text: me asking it to do things more specifically is another way of uploading reference data
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: The value of AI outreach is the research before the email, not the sending.

quote.text: the magic is not in cold emailing. It's in all the research it's doing beforehand.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Sell to people who already value the thing (those with a website, clean driveways), not those who plainly need it but don't care.
Use research agents to validate demand cheaply by mining reviews, Reddit and YouTube before building a product.
Once you have proprietary data from an agent, keep questioning it to find which problems are widespread.
Speed of adoption matters: people who automate workflows early gain a cost advantage over those treating AI as a search engine.

quote.text: the gap between the people who just get this and the people who don't is about to become as big as the Grand Canyon.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Platform risk: features absorbed by OpenAI can erase wrapper businesses.
Agent tools remain slow and glitchy for multi-login tasks, so plan for human supervision.

evidence_quality.rationale: Live demo of a tool by a host with no verified business results for these ideas; he rates outputs subjectively, and the figures are agent-found or hearsay. Hype-heavy framing, with the one first-hand business (Texas Snacks) given no numbers.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes his paid TK Owners community ($99/month) and his newsletter/podcast; says he is not sponsored by OpenAI.
